en.headline: Three arrested, 1,600 unregistered vials seized in vaccine-related raids
en.dek: Health Secretary Lo Chung-mau said none of the seized items were the touted WT1 cancer-prevention product; no reports of anyone receiving the injection locally.
body: Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau said on Saturday that more than 1,600 vials of unregistered injectable products had been seized in joint raids by the Department of Health and police on 14 premises.

Three people in charge of the premises were arrested, including one doctor. None of the seized vials contained the so-called WT1 vaccine that some health centres had promoted online as capable of preventing multiple cancers.

Lo told an RTHK radio programme that there is no such pharmaceutical product registered in Hong Kong, on the mainland or overseas. He said evidence showed some people had purchased the claimed product, but there have been no reports of anyone receiving the injection in Hong Kong. Recipients, if any, may have been non-residents who have since left.

He warned that injecting unregistered products carries severe risks because the substances enter the bloodstream directly. Previous cases of contaminated health products had caused bacterial infections. The Department of Health has stressed that any promotion claiming an unregistered product can prevent cancer is misleading.

zh.headline: 無牌針劑搜查拘三人 檢獲一千六百劑未經註冊製品
zh.dek: 醫務衞生局局長盧寵茂表示檢獲物品並非聲稱的WT1防癌疫苗，暫無發現有人在港注射。
body: 醫務衞生局局長盧寵茂今日表示，衞生署聯同警方搜查十四個處所，檢獲超過一千六百劑未經註冊的注射製品，三人被捕，其中一人為醫生。
檢獲物品並非早前有醫療中心在網上宣傳、聲稱可預防多種癌症的WT1疫苗。盧寵茂指，香港、內地及海外均無此類註冊藥劑製品。
他在電台節目表示，有證據顯示有人曾購買相關產品，但至今未發現有人在港注射，亦不排除購買或注射者為境外人士。
盧寵茂警告，注射未經註冊製品風險極高，因為物質直接進入血液。過往曾有保健注射製品受污染導致細菌入血的個案。衞生署強調，任何聲稱未經註冊製品可防癌的宣傳均屬誤導。
